  
PROJECT PROPOSAL

**CodeImpact AI**

*An LLM-Based Repository Change Impact Analyzer*

CSE 4011 — Intelligent Developer Tools and AI DevOps Workflows

Academic Year 2026–27  |  7th Semester

# **1\. Project Charter / Synopsis**

| Field | Details |
| :---- | :---- |
| Project Title | CodeImpact AI — An LLM-Based Repository Change Impact Analyzer |
| Problem | Developers cannot easily tell which files, functions, modules, APIs, or tests a proposed code change may affect, since keyword or dependency search misses semantic relationships in the codebase. |
| Proposed Solution | A Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system that indexes a repository, retrieves the code, tests, and docs most relevant to a proposed change, and uses Code Llama (via Ollama) to generate an evidence-grounded impact report. |
| Target Users | Software developers, development teams, DevOps engineers, and teams maintaining large or fast-evolving repositories. |
| Knowledge / Data Source | An open-source GitHub repository — source code, functions/classes, test files, documentation, README files, and API definitions. |
| Core Technologies | React, FastAPI, LangChain, Ollama \+ Code Llama, ChromaDB/FAISS, GitHub Actions, Docker. |
| Expected Output | A Change Impact Report listing affected components, risk level, a natural-language explanation, and recommended tests. |
| Advanced Extension | GitHub Actions integration that triggers CodeImpact AI on every pull request and runs the recommended tests automatically. |

# **2\. Problem Statement**

Modern software repositories are made up of many interconnected files, functions, APIs, modules, and test cases. A seemingly small code change can unintentionally affect components that are not obviously related to it. Developers typically inspect the repository manually to judge the blast radius of a change, and existing tools — keyword search or static dependency analysis — surface direct references but miss semantic relationships between different parts of the codebase.

Example: a change to calculateStudentCredits() may affect Course Registration, Examination, Academic Reports, and their related test cases, even though none of those modules directly import the changed function by name.

*Research Question: Can LLM-based semantic understanding, combined with Retrieval-Augmented Generation, improve the accuracy of software change-impact analysis compared with conventional keyword and dependency-based approaches?*

# **3\. Objectives and Expected Outcomes**

* Build a RAG pipeline that indexes an entire repository (code, tests, documentation) into a searchable vector store.

* Given a natural-language change description, a code diff, or a modified file, retrieve the repository content most semantically related to that change.

* Use Code Llama (via Ollama) to reason over the retrieved context and generate an evidence-grounded impact report — not a guess from general programming knowledge alone.

* Classify impact by risk level (High / Medium / Low) and recommend the specific tests that should be re-run.

* Package the pipeline behind a FastAPI backend and a React dashboard so it is usable as a real developer tool, not just a script.

* (Advanced) Trigger the analysis automatically on GitHub pull requests via GitHub Actions and post the impact report as a PR comment.

* Evaluate the system quantitatively — precision, recall, F1 — against a traditional keyword-search baseline, giving the project a measurable research component.

# **4\. Proposed Solution and Use Case**

CodeImpact AI is an LLM-powered application that analyzes a developer's proposed code change and predicts which parts of a repository may be affected. The repository is collected, chunked into meaningful code units, converted into vector embeddings, and stored in a vector database. When a developer submits a change, the system semantically searches this index, retrieves the most relevant code, tests, and documentation, and passes that context to Code Llama to generate the final report.

## **4.1 Input**

* A natural-language description of a proposed change

* A code change / snippet

* A Git diff

* A modified file

## **4.2 Worked Example**

|  | Content |
| :---- | :---- |
| Input | Changed File: authentication.pyChange: Modified password validation rules to require stronger passwords. |
| Output — High Impact | login.py, user\_service.py, password\_reset.py |
| Output — Recommended Tests | test\_login.py, test\_authentication.py, test\_password\_reset.py |
| Output — Risk Level | HIGH |
| Output — Explanation | The modified password validation logic is directly related to authentication and password-reset workflows. |

# **5\. Knowledge / Data Source**

The knowledge base is the target repository itself, so the LLM reasons over real project context instead of only its pre-trained general knowledge.

| Data Source | Purpose |
| :---- | :---- |
| Source Code | Understand application functionality |
| Functions and Classes | Identify semantic relationships between components |
| Test Files | Recommend the tests relevant to a change |
| Documentation | Understand project-specific requirements |
| README Files | Understand overall architecture |
| API Definitions | Identify potentially affected APIs |
| Git History (advanced stage) | Understand the history of previous related changes |

*Initial scope: Source Code \+ Tests \+ Documentation from a single open-source GitHub repository.*

# **7\. Working Flow of the Project (RAG Pipeline)**

The pipeline has two halves that run on different triggers: repository indexing happens once (and again on new commits), while the query-and-impact-analysis flow runs every time a developer submits a change.

![][image2]

*Figure 2 — Repository indexing flow and query/retrieval flow*

## **7.1 Step-by-step**

* Repository is collected and relevant files (code, tests, docs) are extracted.

* Files are split into meaningful chunks (functions, classes, doc sections).

* Each chunk is converted into a vector embedding and stored in the vector database (ChromaDB/FAISS).

* When a developer submits a change, it is converted into a query embedding.

* A vector similarity search retrieves the most relevant code, tests, and documentation.

* The retrieved context plus the original change is assembled into a prompt for Code Llama.

* Code Llama returns affected components, risk level, an explanation, and recommended tests.

* The report is shown on the web dashboard and, at the advanced stage, posted back to the GitHub pull request.

# **8\. Technology Stack**

| Layer | Technology | Purpose |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Frontend | React | User interface / dashboard |
| Backend | FastAPI | Application APIs |
| Programming Language | Python | RAG pipeline and backend development |
| LLM Runtime | Ollama | Running the LLM locally |
| LLM | Code Llama | Code understanding and impact analysis |
| RAG Framework | LangChain | Retrieval and LLM orchestration |
| Chunking | Code / text splitters | Splitting repository files into meaningful units |
| Embeddings | Ollama Embeddings / Sentence-Transformers | Converting code into vectors |
| Vector Database | ChromaDB | Storing and retrieving embeddings |
| Alternative Vector Search | FAISS | Optional vector similarity implementation |
| Repository | GitHub | Source code and version control |
| Testing | PyTest / project-specific framework | Testing affected components |
| CI/CD | GitHub Actions | Automated workflow execution on pull requests |
| Containerization | Docker | Packaging application and services |

# **9\. Phase-wise Development Plan**

The application is built progressively across the semester, in line with the course's Project-Based Learning structure.

| Phase | Goal | Key Concepts / Technologies |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Phase 1 | Basic LLM-based impact analysis from a plain-text change description | Code Llama, Ollama, prompt engineering |
| Phase 2 | Wrap the prototype in a real application and API layer | React, FastAPI, Python, REST APIs |
| Phase 3 | Make the LLM repository-aware by building the RAG knowledge base | LangChain, repository indexing, chunking, ChromaDB |
| Phase 4 | Retrieve semantically related code and predict impact | Embeddings, vector similarity, ChromaDB/FAISS |
| Phase 5 | Automate validation as part of the DevOps workflow | Testing, GitHub Actions, CI/CD, Docker |

# **12\. Feasibility and Resource Planning**

* All core tools (Ollama, Code Llama, ChromaDB/FAISS, LangChain, FastAPI, React) are free and open-source, so the project has no licensing cost.

* Code Llama runs locally through Ollama, avoiding dependency on paid, rate-limited external APIs during development and grading demos.

* The team's 3-member split (RAG / Backend / Frontend+DevOps) matches the university's required team size of 3–5 with clear role distribution.

* Scope is deliberately staged: a working, demonstrable subset exists after every phase (Phase 1 already shows an end-to-end demo, even before RAG is added).

* Risks: local LLM inference speed on limited hardware, and embedding quality on very large repositories — both mitigated by starting with a small, well-scoped open-source repository for Phases 1–4.

# **. Final Proposal Statement**

CodeImpact AI is an AI-powered developer tool that analyzes the potential impact of code changes within a software repository. It combines Retrieval-Augmented Generation, semantic code retrieval, embeddings, vector similarity search, and Code Llama to identify potentially affected files, functions, modules, APIs, and tests. The project evolves progressively — from a basic LLM-based prototype into a repository-aware RAG system integrated with automated testing and GitHub Actions-based CI/CD — mirroring the phase-wise structure of the CSE 4011 course.
